objects.taxonomy_description: Cylindrical stick of wax (15-30 cm tall, 2-5 cm diameter) with a central wick (cotton string) extending from the top. The wax body is smooth and uniform, available in white, ivory, or colored varieties. The surface has a matte or slightly glossy finish depending on wax type (paraffin, beeswax, soy). The top has a charred wick tip if previously burned. Taper candles narrow toward the top; pillar candles maintain uniform diameter. The base is flat for standing. Scented candles may have a slightly textured surface from fragrance oils. The overall shape is a simple vertical cylinder with a thin wick protruding from the center.

objects.taxonomy_description: The giraffe is distinguished by its exceptionally long neck and legs, unique ossicone head structures, and characteristic coat patterns.

diagnostic_checkpoints.Neck_Length: The animal possesses an extremely elongated neck that is significantly longer than its torso.
diagnostic_checkpoints.Leg_Proportions: The forelegs are notably long and slender, contributing to a steeply sloping back profile.
diagnostic_checkpoints.Head_Structure: The head features distinct, skin-covered bony protrusions known as ossicones rather than branched antlers or hollow horns.
diagnostic_checkpoints.Coat_Pattern: The body is covered in large, irregular polygonal patches separated by lighter-colored lines.

objects.taxonomy_description: Stringed instrument with solid or semi-hollow body (no sound hole required). Body shape varies: Stratocaster (double-cutaway, contoured edges), Les Paul (single-cutaway, carved top), Telecaster (single-cutaway, slab body). Body is wood (alder, mahogany, maple) with glossy polyester or nitrocellulose finish in solid colors, sunburst, or natural wood grain. Neck is maple or mahogany with fretted fingerboard (rosewood or maple, 21-24 frets). Pickups (magnetic, 1-3) mounted on body. Control knobs (volume, tone) and pickup selector switch. Bridge is fixed or tremolo. Headstock has 6 tuning pegs. Cable jack on body edge.
